# nish/net/oidc

Verify a JWT from an OpenID Connect issuer: find the issuer's keys through discovery (OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0), read its JWK Set (RFC 7517, RFC 7518 §6, RFC 8037), follow its key rotation, and check a token's signature and claims with `nish/crypto/jwt`.

```ts
import {
  OIDC_DEFAULT_LEEWAY,
  OIDC_DEFAULT_LIFETIME,
  OIDC_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS,
  OIDC_ERR_DUPLICATE_KID,
  OIDC_ERR_FETCH,
  OIDC_ERR_ISSUER,
  OIDC_ERR_JSON,
  OIDC_ERR_KEY,
  OIDC_ERR_KID_REQUIRED,
  OIDC_ERR_NO_KEYS,
  OIDC_ERR_PRIVATE,
  OIDC_ERR_SCHEME,
  OIDC_ERR_SIZE,
  OIDC_ERR_STALE,
  OIDC_ERR_TOO_MANY_KEYS,
  OIDC_ERR_UNKNOWN_KID,
  OIDC_MAX_DISCOVERY_BYTES,
  OIDC_MAX_JWKS_BYTES,
  OIDC_MAX_KEYS,
  OIDC_MAX_KID,
  OIDC_MAX_LIFETIME,
  OIDC_MIN_LIFETIME,
  OIDC_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL,
  OIDC_OK,
  OIDC_SKIPPED,
  OIDC_STALE_GRACE,
  OidcKeySet,
  OidcKeys,
  OidcMetadata,
  OidcOptions,
  oidcDiscover,
  oidcDiscoveryUrl,
  oidcHttpOptions,
  oidcIssuerAllowed,
  oidcLifetime,
  oidcParseDiscovery,
  oidcParseJwks,
  oidcVerify,
} from "nish/net/oidc";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { OIDC_OK, OidcKeys, OidcMetadata, OidcOptions, oidcDiscover, oidcVerify } from "nish/net/oidc"

const options = new OidcOptions()
const meta: OidcMetadata = oidcDiscover("https://issuer.example", options) // once, at start-up
const keys = new OidcKeys(meta, options)
keys.refresh(now) // fetch the key set; then call refresh(now) from the server's own timer
if (oidcVerify(keys, token, "my-api", now) === OIDC_OK) {
  const claims: string = keys.claimsText()
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-detail title="Nothing is guessed about the issuer">

The issuer is named by the caller,
and the discovery document must name the same issuer, byte for byte; the key
set is read only from the `jwks_uri` that document gives, and both must be
https (loopback http, with `allowLoopbackHttp`, for an http issuer only). A
`jwks_uri` on another origin than the issuer's was chosen by the document,
not the program, so it is fetched under an `OutboundPolicy`
(`OidcOptions.jwksOutbound`): public addresses only, no proxy. Every key in
the set is bound to exactly one algorithm, which comes
from the key — its `kty`, its `crv` and its `alg` — and never from a token's
header: a key whose `alg` disagrees with its type refuses the whole set, and
the verifier refuses a token whose header names any other algorithm.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Fetches are synchronous and happen only where the caller asks">

`oidcDiscover` and `OidcKeys.refresh` each make one blocking GET, bounded by
`OidcOptions.timeoutMs`; `OidcKeys.key` and `oidcVerify` never fetch. A
token with a `kid` the set does not hold marks the set as wanted, so the
next `refresh` fetches it early, at most once per
`OIDC_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`. A server calls `refresh(now)` from its own
loop or timer, where blocking is harmless, and never from a request.

</scalar-detail>

Every function that reads the clock takes it as a `now` parameter, in
seconds since 1970, so a test drives the clock; `oidcDiscover` reads none. The security record is `docs/security/oidc.md`.

@module

### oidcDiscover

followed, bounded by `options.timeoutMs` and `OIDC_MAX_DISCOVERY_BYTES`,

  issuer: string,
  options: OidcOptions,

### oidcLifetime

How long a key set fetched with this `Cache-Control` is fresh: its first
`max-age` directive of plain digits, clamped to `[OIDC_MIN_LIFETIME,
OIDC_MAX_LIFETIME]`, or `OIDC_DEFAULT_LIFETIME` when there is none. Other

### oidcParseJwks

A JWK Set, already fetched, read into keys. The rules:

- The document is at most `OIDC_MAX_JWKS_BYTES`, a JSON object whose `keys`
  is an array of at most `OIDC_MAX_KEYS` entries.

Each entry is then read by these rules, in this order; the first that
applies decides it, and a refusal refuses the whole set:

1. An entry that is not an object refuses the set (`OIDC_ERR_JSON`).
2. An entry holding `d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `oth` or `k` refuses the
   set (`OIDC_ERR_PRIVATE`), whatever its `use` or type: a publisher that
   leaks a private or symmetric key has a set no verifier should trust.
3. An entry without `kty`, or whose `kty`, `use`, `alg`, `kid` or `crv` is
   present and not a string, refuses the set (`OIDC_ERR_JSON`).
4. A `kid` that is not 1 to `OIDC_MAX_KID` bytes of printable ASCII refuses
   the set (`OIDC_ERR_KEY`), whatever the entry's `use`.
5. An entry whose `use` is present and not `"sig"` is skipped.
6. An entry whose `alg` names an algorithm `nish/crypto/jwt` does not have
   is skipped.
7. An entry whose `kty`/`crv` is not RSA, EC P-256, EC P-384 or OKP Ed25519
   is skipped when it has no `alg`, and refuses the set (`OIDC_ERR_KEY`)
   when it has one, since the `alg` then names a key this module would
   misread.
8. The key's algorithm is its `alg` when present, which must agree with its
   type (RS256/384/512 for RSA, ES256 for P-256, ES384 for P-384, EdDSA for
   Ed25519), or the set is refused (`OIDC_ERR_KEY`); without `alg` it is
   ES256, ES384 or EdDSA by curve, and RS256 for RSA, OpenID Connect Core's
   default.
9. The key's material must make a key — `n`/`e` with an RSA modulus of 2048
   to 8192 bits, `x`/`y` of the curve's size, an Ed25519 `x` of 32 bytes —
   or the set is refused (`OIDC_ERR_KEY`).

Then:

- Two keys taken with the same `kid`, or two without one, refuse the set
  (`OIDC_ERR_DUPLICATE_KID`), and a set where none is taken is
  `OIDC_ERR_NO_KEYS`.

```ts
const oidcParseJwks: (doc: u8[]) => OidcKeySet
```

<scalar-field name="doc" type="u8[]" required>

The JWK Set's bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="OidcKeySet">

The set; its `error` is `OIDC_OK` or the reason it was refused.

</scalar-field>

### oidcVerify

Verify `token` with the issuer's keys, without fetching. The key is chosen
by the token's `kid`; a token with no `kid` — or one whose `kid` is not a
string or is longer than `OIDC_MAX_KID`, which counts as none — is taken
only when the set holds exactly one key, and is checked under that key,
since otherwise which key it means is a guess. The key
alone decides the algorithm, so `none`, any HMAC algorithm and any
algorithm but the key's are refused (`JWT_ERR_ALG`); then the signature,
`iss` (the issuer, exactly), `aud` (a string or an array that holds
`audience`), and `exp`, `nbf` and `iat` within `options.leeway` are checked
by `nish/crypto/jwt`'s `JwtVerifier`, and `exp` is required.

```ts
const oidcVerify: (
  keys: OidcKeys,
  token: string,
  audience: string,
  now: i64,
) => i32
```

<scalar-field name="keys" type="OidcKeys" required>

The issuer's keys.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="token" type="string" required>

The compact token.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="audience" type="string" required>

The audience the token must name: this service's client id.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="now" type="i64" required>

The current time, in seconds since 1970.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

`OIDC_OK` (`JWT_OK`), an `OIDC_ERR_*` when no key could be chosen,
  or the `JWT_ERR_*` the verifier refused the token with.

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### OidcKeySet

A JWK Set as taken: each key bound to one algorithm, with its `kid`, or why the set was refused.

```ts
class OidcKeySet
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new OidcKeySet()` | An empty set, `OIDC_OK`; `oidcParseJwks` is the way to fill one. |
| `error: i32` | `OIDC_OK`, or the reason the set was refused; a refused set holds no key. |
| `keys: JwtKey[]` | The keys taken, in the set's order. |
| `kids: string[]` | Each key's `kid`; `""` for a key with none. |
| `count(): i32` | The number of keys taken. |
| `find(kid: string): JwtKey \| null` | The key whose `kid` is `kid`, spelled exactly. |

### OidcKeys

An issuer's rotating key set, and a verifier for its tokens. One thread's,
like the `JwtVerifier` it holds.

The set is fetched by `refresh`, which fetches only when it is due: there
is no set yet, the set is past its lifetime (`oidcLifetime`), or a token
named a `kid` the set does not hold — and never twice within
`OIDC_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`. A refresh that fails keeps the last set taken,
which keeps verifying until `OIDC_STALE_GRACE` past the end of its
lifetime; past that hard expiry, nothing verifies until a refresh succeeds.
A refresh that succeeds replaces the set whole, so a key the issuer stopped
publishing stops verifying then. A token whose `kid` the set holds never
makes a refresh due early, so a removed key keeps verifying until the set's
lifetime ends — at most `OIDC_MAX_LIFETIME` — and, while refreshes fail,
until its hard expiry, at most `OIDC_STALE_GRACE` more.

```ts
class OidcKeys
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new OidcKeys(meta: OidcMetadata, options: OidcOptions)` | Keys for the issuer `meta` names; nothing is fetched until `refresh`. |
| `freshUntil: i64` | When the last set taken stops being fresh. |
| `hardUntil: i64` | When the last set taken stops verifying, if no refresh replaces it. |
| `lastError: i32` | The result of the last refresh that fetched: `OIDC_OK` or why it failed. |
| `readonly meta: OidcMetadata` | The issuer's metadata, as discovery gave it. |
| `readonly options: OidcOptions` | The options fetches and verification use. |
| `set: OidcKeySet \| null` | The last set taken, or null before the first. |
| `tried: boolean` | Whether any fetch has been begun. |
| `triedAt: i64` | When the last fetch was begun. |
| `readonly verifier: JwtVerifier` | The verifier `oidcVerify` uses; after `OIDC_OK`, its `claims`, `exp` and `nbf` are the token's. |
| `wanted: boolean` | Whether a token named a `kid` the set does not hold since the last fetch. |
| `check(key: JwtKey, n: i32, audience: string, now: i64): i32` | Verify the token `load` copied under `key`, against the issuer and `audience`. |
| `claimsText(): string` | The claims of the last token `oidcVerify` accepted, as text. |
| `due(now: i64): boolean` | Whether `refresh(now)` would fetch: there is no set, the set is past its lifetime, or a token wanted a `kid` it lacks — and the last fetch began at least `OIDC_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL` ago (or later than `now`, after the clock stepped back). |
| `key(kid: string, now: i64): JwtKey \| null` | The key whose `kid` is `kid`, without fetching. A `kid` the set lacks marks the set as wanted, so the next due `refresh` fetches it. |
| `load(token: string): i32` | The token's bytes in the verifier's buffer, for `oidcVerify`. |
| `peekKid(n: i32): string \| null` | The `kid` of the token `load` copied, read before any signature is checked, only to choose a key. |
| `refresh(now: i64): i32` | Fetch the key set from `meta.jwksUri` when a refresh is due: one blocking GET, no redirect followed, bounded by `options.timeoutMs` and `OIDC_MAX_JWKS_BYTES`, and under `options.jwksOutbound` when the `jwks_uri` is on another origin than the issuer. Call it once at start-up and then from the server's own loop or timer. |
| `refreshWith(doc: u8[] \| null, cacheControl: string \| null, now: i64): i32` | Take `doc` as the key set when a refresh is due, without fetching: for a caller that fetches the set its own way, and for tests. Counts as a fetch for the rate limit. |
| `usable(now: i64): boolean` | Whether the set verifies at `now`: one has been taken and it is not past its hard expiry. |

### OidcMetadata

What discovery found: the issuer as configured and the URL of its key set, or why it failed.

```ts
class OidcMetadata
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new OidcMetadata(error: i32, issuer: string, jwksUri: string)` | Metadata from its parts, checked for nothing; `oidcDiscover` and `oidcParseDiscovery` are the way to make one. |
| `error: i32` | `OIDC_OK`, or the reason discovery failed; the other fields are empty unless it is `OIDC_OK`. |
| `issuer: string` | The issuer, as configured and as the document named it. |
| `jwksUri: string` | The document's `jwks_uri`. |

### OidcOptions

How discovery and the key set fetch, and how tokens are checked.

```ts
class OidcOptions
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new OidcOptions()` | The defaults: `OIDC_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `OIDC_DEFAULT_LEEWAY`, `JWT_MAX_TOKEN`, no loopback http, and a default `OutboundPolicy` for a `jwks_uri` on another origin. |
| `allowLoopbackHttp: boolean` | Allow `http://` to `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `::1` for the issuer and `jwks_uri`; off by default, for tests. |
| `jwksOutbound: OutboundPolicy \| null` | The policy a `jwks_uri` on another origin than the issuer's is fetched under, since the discovery document chose it and the program did not: by default `new OutboundPolicy()`, public addresses only and no proxy. Null fetches it like the issuer, through any proxy the environment names. |
| `leeway: i64` | The clock skew allowed on `exp`, `nbf` and `iat`, in seconds. |
| `maxToken: i32` | The longest token verified, in bytes. |
| `timeoutMs: i32` | The bound on one fetch, connect to last byte, in milliseconds; 0 or less means `OIDC_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="65,536" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_MAX_DISCOVERY_BYTES: i32`

The largest discovery document read, in bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="65,536" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_MAX_JWKS_BYTES: i32`

The largest JWK Set read, in bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="64" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_MAX_KEYS: i32`

The most entries a JWK Set's `keys` may list, taken or skipped.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="256" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_MAX_KID: i32`

The longest `kid`, in bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="86,400" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_MAX_LIFETIME: i64`

The longest a key set is fresh, in seconds, whatever `max-age` says.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="300" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_MIN_LIFETIME: i64`

The shortest a key set is fresh, in seconds, whatever `max-age` says.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="60" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL: i64`

The least time between two fetches of the key set, in seconds. A fetch
clears the unknown-`kid` mark as it begins, so one that fails is tried
again only when another unknown `kid` arrives or the set's lifetime ends,
not merely once this interval has passed.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-41" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_ERR_SIZE: i32`

The document is larger than its limit (`OIDC_MAX_DISCOVERY_BYTES`, `OIDC_MAX_JWKS_BYTES`).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-52" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_ERR_STALE: i32`

No key set has been taken yet, or the last one is past its hard expiry.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-48" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_ERR_TOO_MANY_KEYS: i32`

The set lists more than `OIDC_MAX_KEYS` keys.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-50" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_ERR_UNKNOWN_KID: i32`

The token's `kid` is not in the set.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_OK: i32`

Success.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_SKIPPED: i32`

`OidcKeys.refresh` did nothing: the set is fresh and wanted by no token, or the last attempt was too recent.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="86,400" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`OIDC_STALE_GRACE: i64`

How long past its freshness a key set still verifies while refreshes fail, in seconds.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
